_doc: THE one tunable file for JUMP PADS (D-JUMPPAD-1..9; DESIGN.md section 3.4). A jump pad is a separate entity from the generator's LAUNCH pads (voidgen W.pads, the 'X' line, controller _try_launch_pad): a launch pad throws the player onto a target tile and is load-bearing for reachability; a jump pad flings the player STRAIGHT UP, keeps their horizontal momentum, and refills their MOVEMENT resources only (air jumps, dash + twin dash, glider energy, updraft, ability lock) - never void charges, gold or the beacon shield. Placement is game/terrain/jump_pads.gd place_jump_pads(level, cfg): a pure function of the Level dict, so the level hash still determines the pads without touching the frozen generator's canonical text. A pad is a size_tiles x size_tiles BLOCK of tiles (3x3, D-JUMPPAD-6) anchored on its centre tile, and it sits OUTSIDE the paths and ADJACENT to them, both as HARD rules (D-JUMPPAD-7): every tile of the block is a FLOOR tile of a platform piece, so no tile is a walkway tile (the path) or a walkway's centre lane (the route), and none is the hub/beacon piece, a stair/step/ramp walkway, a ramp tile, a prop, a gift slot, a tripmine slot, a launch pad or its landing tile; AND at least one tile EDGE-adjacent to the block - the 4-neighbourhood of its 9 cells, never a diagonal - is a walkway tile within path_step_hu vertically. A block with no such neighbour is not a candidate at all, so a pad can never sit out on a platform away from every path. Candidates are taken in the pad RNG stream's shuffled order, greedily with min_spacing_tiles. count_by_level: the row with the largest 'from' <= the level number gives the pad count (2 at level 1 up to 6 on big levels; fewer are placed when the level has fewer legal spots, never more). min_spacing_tiles: the XZ distance between any two pad anchors is at least this. 4 is the smallest spacing that leaves a gap between two 3x3 blocks (centres 4 apart = one empty tile between); 8 was tried and cost pads on the big levels (level 20 average 5.25 instead of 5.50) without helping the floor of 2 anywhere, and the old 12 was tuned for 1-tile pads. path_step_hu: how far above or below a pad's height a walkway tile may sit and still count as the path beside it. The generator steps a walkway 1-2 HU off the platform it runs beside at the junction, so a path tile is almost never at the same height as the platform floor next to it: over 20 seeds x 8 levels there are 23 same-height path/floor edge pairs in 160 levels against 2127 at +1 HU and 1257 at +2 HU, and a same-height rule leaves 0 legal blocks on 5 of the 8 level sizes. 4 covers the junction step and the first stair row and stays well under CLEAR (12 HU), so a walkway on another storey can never satisfy it. launch_speed: the upward velocity in u/s set on trigger; under gravity 32 the apex is v^2/64 = 6.25 u at 20.0 (a normal jump is 12.0 -> 2.25 u; a stair walkway climbs at most 3 u, so 6.25 u clears about two stair walkways' worth) and the air time to land back on the pad's height is 2v/32 = 1.25 s. rearm_s: after a pad fires it is inert for this long (rounded to whole 60 Hz ticks), so standing on it cannot chain-fire; landing back on it after a full 1.25 s flight re-fires it, which is the point of a pad.
